# homarr_invites (Data Source)

Lists the registration invites Homarr holds — every invite that has not been used or deleted, including expired ones, which Homarr never removes on its own. Requires an admin API key and the `credentials` auth provider.

Useful in a `check` block, for example to flag expired invites left behind, or to find the id of an invite created in the UI so it can be imported as a `homarr_invite`. Tokens are never listed: Homarr returns an invite's token only once, when it is created.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "homarr_invites" "all" {}

# Homarr never deletes expired invites on its own.
check "no_expired_invites" {
  assert {
    condition     = length([for invite in data.homarr_invites.all.invites : invite.id if invite.expired]) == 0
    error_message = "Homarr holds expired invites; delete them or let Terraform manage them."
  }
}

output "open_invite_ids" {
  value = [for invite in data.homarr_invites.all.invites : invite.id if !invite.expired]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `invites` (Attributes List) All invites, ordered by expiration date, soonest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--invites))

<a id="nestedatt--invites"></a>
### Nested Schema for `invites`

Read-Only:

- `creator_id` (String) Identifier of the user that created the invite.
- `creator_name` (String) Name of the user that created the invite.
- `expiration_date` (String) Moment the invite stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC such as `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- `expired` (Boolean) Whether `expiration_date` had passed when the data source was read, by the clock of the machine running Terraform. Homarr refuses an expired invite but keeps it.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the invite.
